title: Kernel limbo: morning scratchpad
content:
Date: 2026-03-13
Context / quick summary:
- Woke up to recurring p99 spikes on inference pool 'serve-gpu-a' overnight. Alerts started ~03:40 PST, repeated every ~45min. Users saw tail latency jumps from ~120ms -> 380-460ms for small-chat workloads. No OOMs, GPU util unchanged.
- Hypothesis: KV cache eviction mis-accounting (LRU index drift) leaving stale prefix entries that cause large KV scans during cache lookup. Might be related to recent change in shard mapping (PR 1982) where we moved to consistent-hash + node-weighting.

Observations from quick triage (what I ran):
- Pulled metrics (prom):
  - inference_request_duration_seconds_p99: 120ms (baseline) -> 420ms at spike
  - kv_cache_hit_ratio: fell from 0.84 -> 0.31 during spikes
  - kv_cache_eviction_rate: near-zero while cache utilization stayed ~82% (suspicious)
- Node-level: on serve-gpu-a-07:
  - nvtop shows stable GPU mem and ~22% GPU util
  - dmesg: no kernel OOM, no PCI resets
  - /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches no activity
- Logs (serving runtime):
  - repeated WARN: "kv_cache: expected eviction candidates none_found" (see log sample below)
  - 1x stacktrace referencing serving_runtime::cache::lru::recompute_index at ~03:40

Log sample snippet (sanitized):
  [2026-03-13T03:40:12Z] WARN kv_cache: expected eviction candidates none_found (pool=serve-gpu-a, shard=3)
  [2026-03-13T03:40:12Z] INFO cache_metrics: size_bytes=524288000 usage_percent=82
  [2026-03-13T03:40:12Z] DEBUG cache_debug: lru_head=null lru_tail=null live_entries=1_023_445

Immediate repro steps (local-ish):
1) Start loadgen with small-chat profile (seq_len ~256, batch 4) against a single-shard model built with the new shard mapping: 
   ./tools/loadgen --model gptx-8k --shard-map tests/shard-maps/consistent-weights.json --qps 450 --duration 600
2) Watch /metrics for kv_cache_* and request latencies. Also tail logs: kubectl -n inference logs -f deployment/serve-gpu-a --since=5m | sed -n '1,200p'
3) Reproduce takes ~3-6 minutes to hit elevated p99 on my laptop sim cluster if map file has skew > 1.6x.

Quick experiment notes I ran (results):
- Repro with skewed map: p99 -> 390ms, kv_hit_ratio -> 0.28.
- Restarting serving-agent (graceful) on a single node temporarily fixed p99 (back to ~130ms) but the issue returned after ~30-40 minutes.
- Forced local evictions via admin endpoint (POST /admin/cache/evict-all) brought hit ratio back to ~0.79 and latencies returned to baseline. Suggests stateful corruption rather than traffic pattern.

Immediate mitigations (short lived):
- If oncall sees spike: roll restart serving-agent on affected pool nodes (order: start with node with WARN logs).
- Expose admin evict endpoint to ops runbook and grant RBAC: evict-all on affected shard.
- Temporary canary config: set shard-weighting back to previous stable map (rollback PR 1982) for the problematic pool until root cause found.

Longer-term next steps / TODOs (with rough estimates):
- [ ] Add invariant asserts in LRU recompute to log more context when "none_found" occurs (owner: Ana, 2d).
- [ ] Add unit test that fuzzes shard-map rebalancing and verifies KV indices remain consistent (owner: Marcus, 3d).
- [ ] Post-mortem / incident report draft (owner: Ana, 1d) -> include timeline, root cause once known, rollback plan.
- [ ] Harden admin evict endpoint with rate-limits and audit logs (owner: Ivy, 2d).
- [ ] Add metric: kv_cache_eviction_candidate_count and instrument more debug states (owner: Marcus, 1d).
- [ ] Run a saturating load test in staging with the new shard-mapper across 24h (owner: eng-qe, 5d).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) LRU index recompute path fails under consistent-hash rebalancing when node weights change: leads to orphaned entries with no eviction pointers -> cache looks full but has no eviction candidates -> eventual scans and long tails. (High)
2) Race between background compaction and eviction background thread where compaction sets head/tail null during resize while eviction reads it (Medium)
3) Under-reporting of live_entries because of integer overflow in path we introduced (low)

Notes-to-self / ops runbook snippet (quick):
- How to run manual eviction: 
  # curl admin endpoint (must be used sparingly)
  curl -X POST "http://serve-gpu-a-07:8080/admin/cache/evict-all" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
- If logs show "none_found": restart serving-agent on node, then run eviction. If still persists, fail over traffic to dedicated fallback pool (route: fallback-lowcost).
- Slack quick ping: #eng-runtime @here with tag RWI-4532 and link to postmortem draft.

Notes for debugging (commands I want to run later):
- kubectl exec -it pod/serve-gpu-a-07 -- /bin/bash -c 'gdb --batch --ex "thread apply all bt" -p $(pidof serving-agent)'
- capture heap snapshot: curl http://localhost:8080/admin/debug/heap > /tmp/heap-$(date +%s).json
- flamegraph: perf record -g -p $(pidof serving-agent) -- sleep 60 ; perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > /tmp/fg.svg

Meeting / handoff notes:
- 09:00 sync with Marcus + Ivy to align triage and who owns tests. Quick agenda: reproduce, run safe evict, prepare rollback plan. (15m)
- Noon: check-in with SRE if /var/lib/inference/cache storage metrics show anomalies.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is eviction logic shared across all model types or per-shard instance? If per-shard, why do multiple shards show same symptom simultaneously?
- Could consistent-hash changes cause cross-shard pointer corruption? Need code walk-through in recompute_index.

Random brain-dump ideas (not necessarily for immediate action):
- Add periodic background scanner that sanity-checks LRU pointers and marks suspects for lazy eviction. Only run in staging first.
- When migration changes shard mapping, run a short 'reindex' cycle that rewrites LRU pointers deterministically before traffic ramps.

End of scratchpad.
- Ana

Quick links I will paste to Slack during triage:

- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1982
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/kv-cache-eviction-postmortem
